```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
    collapse = TRUE,
    comment = "#>"
)
options(ABCatlasR.download_progress = FALSE)
# Cache the vignette's downloads in the session's temporary directory
# rather than the user's cache folder.
options(ABCatlasR.download_base = file.path(tempdir(), "ABCatlasR-cache"))
```

`ABCatlasR` provides an R-native, release-aware interface to the
[Allen Brain Cell (ABC)
Atlas](https://portal.brain-map.org/atlases-and-data/bkp/abc-atlas).

The ABC Atlas, from the Allen Institute, brings together whole-brain
single-cell, single-nucleus and spatial transcriptomics datasets from the
mouse, human, macaque and marmoset brain, together with their cell type
taxonomies. Its H5AD expression matrices and CSV metadata files are
distributed through a public Amazon S3 bucket that requires no account.
`ABCatlasR` lets R users find these datasets, select cells and genes from
their metadata, check the size of a request before downloading, and read
the selected expression into R.

The package separates metadata discovery from expression transfer:

1.  `list_datasets()` discovers curated dataset routes.
2.  `load_data()` loads the cell and gene metadata of a dataset.
3.  `plan_fetch()` reports the expression files a selection of cells
    needs, their sizes and the disk space required. It is optional.
4.  `fetch_data()` downloads and reads the expression of the selected
    cells and genes into the requested R representation.

## Installation

Install the package with `BiocManager`:

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE)) {
    install.packages("BiocManager")
}
BiocManager::install("ABCatlasR")
```

Then load it:

```{r library}
library(ABCatlasR)
```

Core metadata and matrix functionality is R-native. The primary output is a
sparse matrix bundle. SingleCellExperiment and SpatialExperiment outputs
are available directly as alternative representations.

## Discovering datasets

Use `list_datasets()` to inspect the curated routes supported by the
package:

```{r list-datasets}
datasets <- list_datasets()
datasets
```

The catalog reports each route's modality, spatial and imputed status,
default representation and available expression representations.

It is also an ordinary data frame:

```{r spatial-datasets}
datasets[datasets$spatial, ]
```

`list_datasets()` reads the package registry only and performs no
network access.

## Loading metadata

`load_data()` loads and assembles cell and gene metadata. It does not
fetch the large expression matrices.

This vignette uses `Zhuang4`, one of four MERFISH datasets from Zhang et
al. (2023). It covers three sagittal sections of an adult mouse brain
measured with a 1,122-gene panel, and its cells are mapped to the whole
mouse brain taxonomy of Yao et al. (2023). The ABC Atlas distributes the
approximately 0.16 million cells that passed the mapping confidence
threshold. Its metadata take about 40 MB and its raw expression about
64 MB.

```{r load-data}
abc <- load_data(dataset = "Zhuang4", release = "20261130")
abc
```

The cell metadata hold one row per cell, with anatomical, donor and
taxonomy annotations and, for this spatial route, the `x`, `y` and `z`
coordinates:

```{r cell-metadata}
head(abc$cell_metadata)
```

The gene metadata hold one row per gene, keyed by `gene_identifier`:

```{r gene-data}
head(abc$gene_data)
```

`unique_values` lists the values found in the main metadata columns,
which helps when choosing cells. The number of values per column and the
first few of each:

```{r unique-values}
lengths(abc$unique_values)
lapply(abc$unique_values, head, n = 3)
```

## Selecting cells and genes

Cells are selected by their `cell_label` and genes by their identifier
or symbol; both are passed to `fetch_data()`. The cells and genes below
are taken from the outputs shown in the previous section.

### Cell selection

Any subset of the cell metadata gives a vector of cell labels. Here,
brain section `Zhuang-ABCA-4.002` and the GABAergic and glutamatergic
cells in it:

```{r cell-selection}
keep <- abc$cell_metadata$brain_section_label %in% "Zhuang-ABCA-4.002" &
    abc$cell_metadata$neurotransmitter %in% c("GABA", "Glut")
cells <- abc$cell_metadata$cell_label[keep]
length(cells)
table(abc$cell_metadata$neurotransmitter[keep])
```

When the desired cells are already known, their labels can be listed
directly. Here, the first three cells of `head(abc$cell_metadata)`:

```{r cell-id-selection}
my_cell_labels <- head(abc$cell_metadata$cell_label, 3)
my_cell_labels
```

When the selected population is still large, a random subset keeps the
request small. `set.seed()` makes the subset reproducible:

```{r cell-sampling}
set.seed(42)
cells_sampled <- sample(cells, 1000)
length(cells_sampled)
```

### Gene selection

Expression rows are keyed by canonical `gene_identifier`. Each requested
gene is matched first against `gene_identifier`, then against the
published source identifier, then against `gene_symbol`, so symbols and
identifiers can be mixed. Here, three genes from `head(abc$gene_data)`
by symbol and Rxrg by its identifier:

```{r gene-selection}
genes <- c("Htr7", "Sema3c", "Itga8", "ENSMUSG00000015843")
abc$gene_data[
    abc$gene_data$gene_symbol %in% genes |
        abc$gene_data$gene_identifier %in% genes,
    c("gene_identifier", "gene_symbol")
]
```

## Planning expression access

Expression files can be several gigabytes. Before downloading them,
`plan_fetch()` reports what a selection of cells needs. It is optional:
`fetch_data()` does not use its result.

```{r plan-fetch}
plan_fetch(abc, cell_ids = cells)
```

The report lists:

-   the resolved ABC Atlas release;
-   the published representation, for example `raw` or `log2`;
-   the number of selected cells;
-   expression files involved;
-   selected-file sizes;
-   whether each file is cached;
-   resumable partial bytes;
-   additional download required;
-   available disk space and the storage check.

Expression files are downloaded whole, so the report does not depend on
the genes. `plan_fetch()` does not download expression matrices.

Before downloading, `fetch_data()` checks the free space of the disk
that holds the cache, whether or not `plan_fetch()` was called. A
download that does not fit is refused, and on the disk the operating
system runs from at least 2 GB must remain free after the download, so
the system keeps room for virtual memory.

## Fetching expression

`fetch_data()` downloads the expression files the selected cells need,
then reads only the selected cells and genes:

```{r fetch-matrix}
x <- fetch_data(
    abc,
    cell_ids = cells,
    genes = genes,
    data_type = "raw",
    return_type = "matrix" # could pick "sce" or "spatial"
)
dim(x$expression)
x$expression[, 1:3]
Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)
x$provenance
```

This returns an `abc_matrix` object containing sparse expression,
selected metadata and provenance. Rows are genes, keyed by
`gene_identifier`, and columns are cells;
`Matrix::rowSums(x$expression > 0)` counts the selected cells in which
each gene is detected. The provenance records the dataset, release,
representation, modality, spatial status and selected dimensions.

Depending on the downstream analysis, choose `data_type = "raw"` for raw
counts or `data_type = "log2"` for the log2-transformed values published
by the ABC Atlas. Without `data_type`, the dataset's default is used:
`raw` where it is published, otherwise `log2`. `list_datasets()` shows
the default and available representations of each route. Each
representation is a separate file, so only one is downloaded. The
spatial HMBA routes publish `batch_normalized` values, which are counts
normalized for differences between batches, and their natural log,
`ln`, instead of `log2`.

With `genes = NULL`, the default, every gene of the expression file is
returned.

## Output representations

`return_type` selects the representation returned by `fetch_data()`:

-   `"matrix"`, the primary output, is the sparse matrix bundle shown
    above.
-   `"sce"` returns a SingleCellExperiment. Raw expression uses a
    `counts` assay. Other representations use an assay of the same
    name, such as `log2`.
-   `"spatial"` returns a SpatialExperiment with the dataset's spatial
    coordinates attached. It is available for routes declared spatial,
    such as `Zhuang4`, and needs the SpatialExperiment package.

SingleCellExperiment and SpatialExperiment objects store the provenance
in object metadata, and SpatialExperiment provenance additionally
records the coordinate columns used.

Seurat and Monocle 3 objects are not built by `ABCatlasR`. Users of
either tool can convert the matrix output with the code below, which
needs the `SeuratObject` package (CRAN) or the `monocle3` package
(GitHub). Both tools expect count data, so use raw expression; `x` above
is raw.

```{r convert-seurat-monocle3, eval=FALSE}
# Seurat: Seurat replaces "_" in feature names, so rename them first.
counts <- x$expression
rownames(counts) <- gsub("_", "-", rownames(counts))
seu <- SeuratObject::CreateSeuratObject(
    counts = counts,
    meta.data = x$cell_metadata
)

# Monocle 3: gene metadata need a gene_short_name column.
gene_metadata <- x$gene_data
gene_metadata$gene_short_name <- gene_metadata$gene_symbol
cds <- monocle3::new_cell_data_set(
    x$expression,
    cell_metadata = x$cell_metadata,
    gene_metadata = gene_metadata
)
```

## Reusing cached data

Downloaded files are reused from the local cache. The report for the same
cells now shows that nothing needs to be downloaded:

```{r reuse-plan}
plan_again <- plan_fetch(abc, cell_ids = cells)
plan_again$total_download
```

Fetching the same request again reads the expression file from the
cache, and the message reports that no download was needed:

```{r reuse-fetch}
x_again <- fetch_data(abc, cell_ids = cells, genes = genes, data_type = "raw")
identical(x$expression, x_again$expression)
```

Other datasets use the same cache. `Zhuang2` is another MERFISH dataset
from Zhang et al. (2023), measured with the same gene panel, so the genes
selected above can be fetched from it too:

```{r second-dataset}
abc2 <- load_data(dataset = "Zhuang2", release = "20261130")
abc2
```

Here, a reproducible random sample of 5,000 cells:

```{r second-fetch}
set.seed(1)
cells2 <- sample(abc2$cell_metadata$cell_label, 5000)
y <- fetch_data(abc2, cell_ids = cells2, genes = genes)
dim(y$expression)
Matrix::rowSums(y$expression > 0)
```

## Cache location and releases

ABC Atlas metadata and expression files can be large. Files are
downloaded once and reused from a local cache.

The cache directory is resolved in this order:

1.  the `download_base` argument of `load_data()`;
2.  `options(ABCatlasR.download_base = ...)`;
3.  the `ABC_ATLAS_CACHE` environment variable;
4.  a per-user package cache directory.

For example, `options(ABCatlasR.download_base = "~/ABCatlasR-cache")` keeps
the cache in a folder of your home directory. The object returned by
`load_data()` records its cache directory, which `plan_fetch()` and
`fetch_data()` reuse.

The package is release-aware. Without `release`, `load_data()` uses
20261130, the ABC Atlas release this version of the package is
validated against. A release can be pinned explicitly for reproducible
analyses, as above, and earlier releases can be requested too, for
example with `load_data("AgingMouse", release = "20260711")`. Release
20261031 renamed the folders of the HMBA routes; `load_data()` reads
earlier releases with the earlier folder names.

After required files are cached, `offline = TRUE` prevents network
access.
